title: The Gang That Staged A Fake Indian Premier League
sources: BBC News (July 2022) 'Fake Indian Premier League busted in Gujarat' - Conmen set up a fake cricket league on a remote farm in Mehsana to scam Russian gamblers.
The Times of India (July 2022) - Laborers were paid 400 rupees a day to wear official IPL team jerseys and play scripted matches streamed live on YouTube.

lines.text: In twenty twenty-two, a gang in Gujarat staged a complete fake Indian Premier League -
lines.caps: In 2022, | a gang in Gujarat | staged a fake IPL | inside a remote farm -

lines.text: and fooled international gamblers out of millions of rupees.
Inside a remote farm in Mehsana, conmen set up a makeshift cricket pitch with halogen floodlights.
They hired twenty-one local farmers and laborers for four hundred rupees a day,
dressing them in replica jerseys of Chennai Super Kings, Mumbai Indians, and Gujarat Titans.
They set up five HD cameras, hired an umpire with a walkie-talkie, and streamed the matches live on YouTube.
To make it look authentic, they blasted fake crowd cheering sound effects through giant speakers,
while a commentator mimicked famous Indian sports broadcasters over the microphone!
Russian gamblers on Telegram placed thousands of dollars in bets on every single delivery.
The organizers would radio the umpire, telling the bowler when to bowl a slow ball and when the batsman should hit a six!
The entire tournament was running smoothly until local police raided the farm right in the middle of the quarter-finals!
